newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: MOTORCYCLING-CORSER CLINCHES WORLD SUPERBIKE TITLE.
newsitem.headline: MOTORCYCLING-CORSER CLINCHES WORLD SUPERBIKE TITLE.

text.p: Australia's Troy Corser clinched his first world superbike championship title on Sunday when he finished third in the first race of the final meeting of the season.
Corser, who was runner-up in last year's championship, led the riders' standings by 26 points going into Sunday's two scheduled 22-lap races at Phillip Island.
The Ducati rider clinched the title when his only challenger, New Zealand's Aaron Slight, crashed on lap 13 of the first race.

Both races were won by 21-year-old Kawasaki rider Anthony Gobert of Australia. Gobert beat Colin Edwards of the United States on a Yamaha by 0.284 second in the first race and Honda rider Slight by 0.109 second in the second race.
"I would have liked to have won the first race but with Anthony and Colin riding quite hard I thought it better to settle for third and make sure of the championship," Corser told reporters.
Corser was forced to return to the pits for repairs shortly after the start of the second race after hitting a seagull.
"After that, I knew I couldn't feature in the results so I just went out to entertain the crowd," Corser said.
Gobert's two wins mean Australian riders have won 13 of the 16 races held in Australia over the past eight years.
"They were two of the best races I've been in," Gobert said.
"When Colin's tyres began to lose grip in the first race I knew I had him, but I wasn't sure I could hold Aaron off in race two as his Honda is pretty fast."
Corser, the first Australian to win the superbike title, finished the 12-round championship with 369 points, 22 clear of Slight.
Ducati rider John Kocinski of the United States was third on 337 and defending champion Carl Fogarty of Britain fourth on 331.
